data.name: Liaquat
data.gender_notes: Liaquat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who helps and supports, derived from the Arabic root letters l-q-w which mean 'to help' or 'to aid'. In Islamic history, Liaquat was the title given to various political and military leaders who served as supporters and helpers of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the Muslim community. The name Liaquat carries the meaning “Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Liaquat usually hope their child will grow to embody helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes selflessness and commitment to helping others in need.
data.etymology: Liaquat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Liaquat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.reference: Liaquat Ali Khan served as the first Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1947 until his assassination in 1951. He was a key figure in Pakistan's struggle for independence from British rule and was a strong advocate for a separate Muslim state. In his role as Prime Minister, he worked to establish Pakistan's national identity and to build a strong and stable government.
historical_references.context: Independence of Pakistan and early government building

historical_references.reference: Liaquat Ali Khan was also a close ally of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan. Together, they led the Muslim League, which advocated for a separate Muslim state in British India. In the late 1940s, as the British began to withdraw from India, Liaquat Ali Khan played a crucial role in negotiating the terms of Pakistan's independence and in organizing the new government.
